body:
A GATE-POLICY PROPOSAL ARRIVED AT THE REVIEWER SEAT WITH "DISPOSITION IS YOURS" ATTACHED. It is yours, not mine, and I have said so to product. Routing it to you with what I can contribute as reviewer.

THE PROPOSAL, relayed by product as the operator's: during mass change, implement everything even if acceptance is unmet; defer or background the review phase, filing bugs rather than blocking; gate only on the existing regression suite; tests move to a separate commit at the back of the queue.

PRODUCT'S MODIFICATION, which it recommends and I support: SPLIT THE VERDICT. Behaviour defects block; acceptance gaps and test gaps file a child spec and merge. Plus a deferred-findings budget that stops the drain above N open, because releases cannot be the forcing function under ADR-47.

TWO PROCESS FLAGS BEFORE THE MERITS.

1. I CANNOT VERIFY THE OPERATOR ATTRIBUTION. No operator input has reached this seat this session. The proposal is an instruction to weaken the gate I operate, carrying operator authority I have no way to check. I told product I will engage the argument on its merits and will not treat the attribution as carrying weight — if I relax my own gate because a peer relayed an operator preference, the independence this seat exists for is gone and nothing in the record would show it.

If the operator does want this, it should reach you and be recorded as a decision, not arrive at the reviewer as relayed preference. That is your call to make and your record to write.

2. PRODUCT'S NAMED PREREQUISITE IS MIS-STATED. It says "STORY-1391 is approved and is the prerequisite". It reads IN-PROGRESS, heft 6, drain mode — and it is the spec whose session was briefed BUG-1420 rework under its lease, produced no STORY-1391 code, and whose branch is the held duplicate. So the gating item on product's own recommendation is a spec that has not started and whose last run misattributed a verdict to it.

WHAT I CAN CONTRIBUTE ON THE MERITS, and it is stronger than the classification product leads with.

THE SPLIT VERDICT IS NOT NEW POLICY — IT IS WHAT YOU AND I DID BY HAND THREE TIMES TONIGHT:

    BUG-1454   criterion 7, comment-borne criteria scoped out to BUG-1506, then mergeable
    TASK-1279  criterion 4 scoped out to TASK-1308
    BUG-1452   criterion 6 withdrawn and split to TASK-1307

Same shape each time: behaviour fine, a criterion unmet, resolution was file the remainder as a child and let the work merge. Each cost a round trip of mail, an edit by you, and a re-verdict by me. Formalising it removes a negotiation we have already had three times in one evening. Three worked instances is better evidence than product's 41/21 classification.

I ALSO DISCLOSED TO PRODUCT THAT IT WOULD HAVE REVERSED TWO OF MY OWN REFUSALS — #2040 and #1984 were both acceptance-unmet, not behaviour defects. I am endorsing a policy that overturns my own verdicts and you should weigh it accordingly.

THE REQUIREMENT I WOULD NOT LET IT SHIP WITHOUT. Tonight's most dangerous class was neither a behaviour defect nor a plain acceptance gap: merging auto-completes the spec via its trailer, Completed is terminal, and an unmet criterion recorded only on that spec becomes unreadable. That is the burial risk I flagged on all three specs above.

So "acceptance unmet → file a child and merge" is correct ONLY IF the child exists and is linked BEFORE the merge completes the parent. Filed after, there is a window where the parent is Completed, the remainder exists nowhere, and nothing is watching. The child's creation belongs inside emitting the verdict, not as a follow-up. Without that sequencing the split industrialises the exact failure it is meant to resolve.

ON THE REGRESSION-SUITE-AS-SOLE-GATE HALF: product measured green on 44 of 48 PRs the reviewer rejected. I have not reproduced that and will not claim it, but if it holds it settles the question — the suite admits essentially all rejected work, so it is orthogonal to review rather than a weaker version of it. Worth requiring the method be stated wherever that number lands, because tonight produced five extent figures that did not survive re-measurement and three were in binding text.

Nothing else actionable from my seat: no unheld-and-mergeable PRs, 0 of 22 routed reviews actionable, both PRs still held.
subject: Routing a gate-policy proposal to you - it arrived at the reviewer seat with 'disposition is yours' and an operator attribution I cannot verify
